issues.legal_issue: A nonparty in possession who claims an independent right in property may seek adjudication of an objection to delivery of possession in the execution proceeding before being dispossessed.
material_facts: A decree directed delivery of vacant possession of mortgaged property, but the objectors were not parties to the suit that produced the decree.
The objectors claimed that they had occupied the shop as tenants since before the mortgage and asserted rights independent of the judgment debtor.
When delivery of vacant possession was sought, the objectors resisted and applied for their objections to be adjudicated under the execution procedure.
The executing court and the High Court rejected the objections without deciding their merits, relying on a Full Bench ruling that a third party could seek adjudication only after dispossession.
issues.conclusion: The Court held that a person in possession claiming an independent right may object before dispossession and have the claim adjudicated by the executing court. It quashed the lower-court orders and directed the executing court to consider and decide the objections after hearing the parties.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order 21, Rules 97(1), 97(2) and 101 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the expression “any person” includes a nonparty claiming an independent right, including a tenant, who resists delivery of possession. The executing court must adjudicate the claim in the execution proceeding; the objector need not await dispossession. Rule 35 concerns removal of persons bound by the decree, while Rule 36 provides for symbolic delivery where property is occupied by a person not bound to relinquish occupancy. The corresponding pre-amendment provisions also permitted adjudication of such a claim under Rules 97 and 99. The Court relied on Noorduddin v. Dr. K.L. Anand and Brahmdeo Chaudhary v. Rishikesh Prasad Jaiswal, and held that the contrary interpretation in Smt. Usha Jain v. Manmohan Bajaj was not good law.

rule.if: execution_proceeding and nonparty_in_possession and claims_independent_right and resists_delivery and seeks_execution_adjudication

predicates.execution_proceeding: A decree-holder is seeking delivery of immovable property through an execution proceeding.
predicates.nonparty_in_possession: A person who was not a party to the decree is in possession of the property.
predicates.claims_independent_right: The person in possession claims a right to the property independent of the judgment debtor.
predicates.resists_delivery: The person in possession resists or obstructs delivery of the property to the decree-holder.
predicates.seeks_execution_adjudication: The person in possession asks the executing court to adjudicate the objection.

issues.definition: When a nonparty in possession claims an independent right, resists delivery in an execution proceeding, and asks the executing court to decide the objection, the objection is adjudicated in that proceeding before dispossession.
